data.body_html:
If you're looking for the best sunset cruise route in Marbella, start at Puerto Banús and head east to Cabopino. This 25-nautical-mile round trip gives you open sea, a calm cove for swimming, and a skyline view of Marbella's Golden Mile as the sun sets behind La Concha. With a 2-hour charter from €749 (all inclusive), it's the most efficient way to experience the Costa del Sol at golden hour.

Why Puerto Banús to Cabopino is the Best Sunset Route

Most sunset cruises hug the coast, but this route adds a proper sea leg. You leave the marina, pass the Marbella skyline, and cruise past sandy beaches until you reach Cabopino – a small, protected cove near the dunes of Artola. The return leg faces west, so you watch the sun drop into the sea with La Concha mountain as a backdrop. It's a route that gives you both adventure and postcard views.

Distance: 12.5 NM each way. At 20–25 knots, you'll spend about 35 minutes each way, leaving plenty of time to drop anchor, swim, and sip cava.

When to Depart for the Perfect Sunset

In June, July, and August, sunset is around 21:30–21:45. Depart Puerto Banús at 18:30–19:00. You'll reach Cabopino with the sun still high, swim for 30–45 minutes, then start back as the light turns golden. In September, sunset shifts to ~20:30, so depart by 18:00.

Your skipper will adjust the exact timing based on the day's weather and light. Aim to be back at the marina just after dark – the lights of Puerto Banús are part of the show.

What You'll See Along the Route

  • Puerto Banús: luxury yachts and the famous marina – a glamorous start.
  • Marbella Beachfront: golden sands and beach clubs like Nikki Beach and Ocean Club.
  • La Concha: the iconic mountain that frames the coast – visible from sea.
  • Cabopino: a quiet cove with turquoise water, ideal for swimming.
  • Artola Dunes: natural sand dunes – a protected area you can view from anchor.

Keep an eye out for dolphins – sightings are common on this stretch, especially in the late afternoon.

Which Boat to Choose for Your Sunset Cruise

For a small group (up to 9–11 people), the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 are the best value. Both are 12.5m flybridge cruisers, and the price is fixed at €749 for 2 hours – that includes skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and VAT. You can extend to 8 hours for €2,299 if you want a longer day.

If you want more space and a free jet ski, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) is a showstopper. Minimum charter is 4 hours at €4,719, but the sunset route can be tailored within that window.

For other boats like the Ferretti 94, Pershing 46, or Lagoon 380, pricing is on request via WhatsApp – we'll tailor a sunset package to your needs.

What's Included on Every Sunset Charter

No hidden extras. Every boat comes with:

  • Licensed skipper (English-speaking)
  • Fuel for the route
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava
  • Light snacks (chips, olives, nuts)
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%) – included in the price

You can bring your own food if you like, but the standard offering is enough for a sunset toast.

How to Make the Most of Your Sunset Cruise

Arrive at Puerto Banús 15 minutes before departure. Wear light layers – it gets cooler on the water after sunset. Bring a camera or phone for the views, and swimwear if you plan to jump in at Cabopino.

If you're celebrating something special (anniversary, proposal, birthday), tell us in advance – we can arrange decorations or a custom playlist. The skipper will anchor at the best spot for the sunset, so you don't have to think about navigation.

Booking Your Sunset Cruise

Ready to secure the best sunset cruise route in Marbella? Contact us via WhatsApp (link on our site) with your preferred date and group size. For the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39, the price is fixed at €749 for 2 hours – no negotiation, no surprises. We'll confirm availability and send a booking link.

If you're planning a larger group or want a longer charter, ask about our full fleet – from the sporty Pershing 46 to the spacious Ferretti 94. All depart from Puerto Banús, so you're never far from the action.
